qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Phase seven. Information theory and compression. This is how files get smaller.
A fixed code gives every letter the same length, three bits each.
A fixed code spends 3 bits on every letter.
So the message B B A D E B C costs twenty-one bits.
That is 21 bits for BBADEBC.
But B turns up three times, and two of its three bits are wasted.
But B turns up three times.
Give B a one bit code, and the total drops to fifteen bits.
Common letters get short codes: 15 bits.
News we expect tells us nothing, so it is worth zero bits.
News we expect tells us nothing: 0 bits.
A one in two chance is one yes or no answer, so one bit.
Half the chance: one yes-or-no answer, 1 bit.
Each time the chance halves, we add one more bit.
Each time the chance halves, one more bit.
The rarer the news, the more it tells us.
Rarer news tells us more.
A source sends four symbols, with chances a half, a quarter, and two eighths.
A source sends four symbols with these chances.
A typical eight has the symbol A four times, B twice, and C and D once.
A typical eight: A four times, B twice.
Each symbol costs its surprise in bits, and the eight add up to fourteen.
Each one costs its surprise in bits.
A fixed two bit code needs sixteen bits. The surprise is only fourteen.
A fixed 2-bit code: 16 bits. Surprise: only 14.
That averages one point seven five bits a symbol. This entropy is the floor for lossless codes.
1.75 bits a symbol: the floor, if nothing is lost.
Codewords are sent with no gaps between them.
Codes sit side by side, with no gaps.
The bits zero one could be the letter A, then B.
01 could be A then B…
Or they could be C. That is two readings.
…or C. Two readings!
The fix is a rule. No code may start another.
Fix it: no code may start another.
Put every code at the end of a branch.
Put every code at a branch end.
Follow the bits down. At a leaf, a letter is done, so this reads A, B, C.
Follow the bits down. A leaf means a letter is done.
So there is only one way to read it.
No code starts another.
Each letter has a chance. Join the two smallest, C and E.
Each letter has a chance. Join the two smallest.
Both letters now sit one step deeper, so they pay one more bit.
Letters under it pay one more bit: +.20.
Repeat with the next two smallest, then the two groups.
Repeat with the two smallest left.
Finally B joins, leaving one node. The tree is done.
One node left: the tree is done.
That averages one point nine eight bits a letter. The floor is one point nine six.
1.98 bits a letter. This source's floor is 1.96.
Common B sits just one step from the root.
Common B sits one step from the root.
The path down to a letter is its code. B gets one bit, the others three.
The path down is the code.
Spell B B A D E B C with these codes, with the fixed code underneath.
Spell BBADEBC with these codes.
The message takes fifteen bits instead of twenty-one.
15 bits instead of 21.
Joined up, the bits still split back into the same codewords.
Joined up, it still splits into the same codes.
L Z W needs no chances. It starts with just the letters A and B.
No chances needed: it starts with just A and B.
If the phrase plus the next letter is new, send a code and learn it.
Phrase plus next letter new? Send a code, learn it.
A B is known, so it grows. A B A is new, so send A B.
Known? Keep growing. New? Send and learn.
Again, grow while known, and send when new.
Same again: grow while known, send when new.
B A is known, then the text ends, so it is sent.
Known again, then the text ends: send it.
So nine letters have become just five codes.
Nine letters became five codes.
Only the codes arrive, with the starting letters A and B.
Only codes arrive, plus the A, B start.
Each code adds an entry, the previous chunk plus this chunk's first letter.
Each code adds an entry: previous plus first letter.
Code four is not in yet. It is A B plus the first letter of A B, so A B A.
Code 4 is not in yet: AB plus AB's first letter.
The text comes back exactly, and no dictionary was ever sent.
Same text back. No dictionary sent.
A GIF packs each row of coloured pixels with L Z W.
A GIF packs each row of pixels with LZW.
L Z W cuts the row into pieces, and each piece gets one code.
Each piece of the row gets one code.
Repeats share codes, so eighteen pixels need only eleven.
Repeats share codes: 18 pixels, 11 codes.
A noisy row hardly repeats, so eighteen pixels still need fifteen codes.
Noise rarely repeats, so it saves little.
L Z W only saves space where the data repeats.
LZW feeds on repeats.
Entropy is the floor for any code that loses nothing.
Huffman merges the two rarest nodes, and repeats.
L Z W learns repeated phrases as it reads.
